claims.text: Great ReFact proposes that products could expose useful capabilities, not only separate application destinations.
Combining capabilities should preserve identities, disagreements and translation losses rather than pretending products have merged.
Cross-product actions require appropriate permissions and should prefer documented interfaces and reversible, user-authorized adapters.
A proposed CoOrbWare interaction is an interface direction, not proof of a native multi-device runtime.
A valid first product augmentation canary should leave vendor-native behavior intact and demonstrate removal or rollback.
Actual time saved, capability gain and independent reader adoption remain hypotheses until measured with appropriate receivers.

purpose: Six human-legible editorial routes over one pinned public Great ReFact source, preserving source facts, consent and recoverable versions.

routes.counterpoint: The simplest improvement might be better built-in app integrations, not an agent layer.
routes.entry: Explore a proposed future where your existing apps remain useful while permitted capabilities connect. No new AI empire is assumed.
routes.headline: You were never supposed to be the operating system.
routes.label: Curious reader
routes.promise: A simple question: could your tools cooperate without turning you into the courier?
routes.task: Read the AI Wars field note; identify one chore you would like to stop relaying manually.

routes.counterpoint: An extra orchestration layer may increase failure modes and maintenance costs.
routes.entry: Try a narrow local UI proposal or API adapter with explicit permission, no hidden keyboard interception and exact receipts.
routes.headline: Compose one capability without taking over the product.
routes.label: Developer
routes.promise: Start with an authorized surface, a testable input and a clean rollback.
routes.task: Inspect the CoPreCursor demo and write down an independent acceptance test.

routes.counterpoint: Some tightly integrated native workflows may outperform cross-vendor composition.
routes.entry: Consider documented capability interfaces, permission checks, export, audit events, rollback and user choice as product advantages.
routes.headline: Your product can stay intact while becoming easier to improve.
routes.label: Vendor or operator
routes.promise: The opportunity is controlled interoperability, not an unauthorized vendor rewrite.
routes.task: Review the Great ReFact checklist; select one reversible pilot with a measurable user benefit.

routes.counterpoint: Observed improvement might result from task familiarity or UI changes, not cross-model intelligence.
routes.entry: Compare an unchanged baseline with an explicitly authorized composed workflow. Report uncertainty, privacy cost and failure cases.
routes.headline: Can composable interfaces reduce human coordination cost?
routes.label: Researcher
routes.promise: A falsifiable question, not an assumed improvement.
routes.task: Define a preregistered task measure and a negative control before declaring synergy.

routes.counterpoint: A polished prototype or published plan is not evidence that people independently use it.
routes.entry: CoCivium has public architectural research and prototypes. A universal CoOrbWare deployment and independent adoption are not established by these source documents.
routes.headline: What exists, what is proposed, and what is missing?
routes.label: Journalist
routes.promise: One source trail with explicit nonclaims and a challenge path.
routes.task: Check the public readiness statement against the architecture. Write one disconfirming question.

routes.counterpoint: A charming diagram can conceal inaccessible controls or ambiguous permissions.
routes.entry: Contrast a sealed app workflow with a permissioned composition of two abilities. Invite learners to identify data ownership, failure recovery and access barriers.
routes.headline: What changes when an app becomes a capability?
routes.label: Educator
routes.promise: A classroom-ready comparison with source checking and space for disagreement.
routes.task: Ask students to distinguish a design claim from one observed fact and one testable prediction.
